This is a pre-produced programme comparison. Your search helped you find the programme; it did not personalize the comparison.

← Back to search

Radboud’s Communication and Information Studies examines language and communication between people, organisations and digital systems. Students study persuasion, organisational and intercultural communication, discourse, digital media and qualitative and quantitative research.

These UCR programmes offer different combinations of rhetoric, media, organisational study, social issues and digital methods. They provide substantial related study but do not reproduce Radboud’s specialist intercultural and communication-analysis sequence, online-reputation course or compulsory bachelor thesis.

Academic year: 2026–2027

External pathway: Dutch CIW; non-abroad pathway; Online Reputation choice

Based on the current regulations. Future course offerings and requirements may change.

What this comparison shows

A curriculum-level comparison of Communication and Information Studies at Radboud University with 3 illustrative UCR study compositions.

CLOSEST UCR MATCH
Closest match to communication & information studies

A broad communication programme joining rhetoric and textual analysis with organisational communication, marketing, visual media and empirical research. It responds to several defining strands of Radboud’s degree, while leaving gaps in specialist intercultural study, conversation analysis and the required thesis.

ADDITIONAL UCR OPTION
Communication for social impact

A public communication route connecting rhetoric and media analysis with climate, health, social movements, environmental justice and civil society. Its empirical and organisational courses support scrutiny of persuasive messages and communication for change.

ADDITIONAL UCR OPTION
Human and digital communication

A communication programme combining rhetoric and media interpretation with human language processing, AI ethics and technical study of digital systems. Programming, neural networks and visual analysis provide complementary computational methods; they do not replace specialist conversation analysis or chatbot evaluation.

Important limitation

This is a curriculum comparison. A UCR composition is not the same disciplinary degree and does not by itself establish a professional qualification or automatic eligibility for a particular master’s programme.

Rows show curricular relationships, including partial matches, rather than course equivalence. A blank cell means there is no closely comparable component in that row. Optional independent research is additional to the displayed 180 EC.

modals.text:
Personal & Professional Development
This course is a first-year requirement and aims to stimulate personal development, namely, being able to actively, consciously and ethically orientate oneself in relation to others and the world. It supports the development of core personal and academic skills that enhance critical thinking and independent learning. It seeks to improve and develop academic writing and presenting skills and helps students develop the foundational skills and attitudes to reflect on societal issues and engage with societal partners.
Close

Introduction to Economics
Explore how individuals, firms, and societies make economic decisions. This course introduces key concepts from both microeconomics and macroeconomics, including markets, incentives, and the principles of supply and demand, and provides a foundation for analyzing real-world economic issues.
Close

Marketing & Consumer Engagement
Marketing & Consumer Engagement examines consumer behaviour, brand strategy and responsible customer engagement. Students analyse case studies, develop marketing plans and consider digital and AI-driven changes in marketing.
Close

Strategy & Digital Transformation
The course explores how companies develop strategies and drive responsible digital transformation amid rapid technology change impacting the economy and society. Students develop a strategic plan, from vision to execution, and identify digital value opportunities. Using industry cases, they gain foresight into digital technologies and their impact on strategy, business models and social responsibilities.
Close

Market Research
See how companies figure out what customers love and what they don’t. You’ll plan and carry out real research, analyze what you find, and share your results. Our course shows you how to gather opinions and turn them into smart business ideas—perfect for future marketers, analysts, or entrepreneurs.
Close

International Business & Governance
This course examines the institutional, political and cultural forces shaping global businesses. It first explores how international companies operate, then centers on key global challenges including cross-border governance, corporate responsibility, geopolitical strategies and global trade. It provides a comprehensive understanding of today’s complex international business environment.
Close

Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations
Through experiential learning, students turn their own bold ideas into new ventures. No prior business expertise is required as teams work on a startup project from ideation to final pitch while gaining business and entrepreneurial skills in areas such as design thinking, business model and customer validation. The class fosters creativity and collaboration to drive business and social innovation.
Close

Research Methods & Statistics
Research Methods & Statistics introduces research design, operationalisation, sampling, experiments and surveys. Students study descriptive and inferential statistics, association, hypothesis testing and analysis of variance, with an introduction to multivariate applications. A group research project applies these methods to a chosen research problem.
Close

Leadership Communication
This course blends theory with practice from both fiction and the real world, helping you develop essential leadership skills. Learn how to inspire teams, sharpen your communication, take ethical decisions, and lead with confidence.
Close

Psychology of Organizations & Leadership
Psychology of Organizations & Leadership examines the psychological, social and structural dynamics of organisations. Case discussions and research-based frameworks address motivation, leadership, group dynamics, organisational culture, power, conflict and change.
Close

Negotiation & Strategic Thinking
How do you get to yes? In this course you will learn how to craft persuasive arguments, deploy the right language, negotiate more effectively, and influence decisions with confidence—whether in business, leadership, or life.
Close

AI Ethics
AI Ethics examines artificial intelligence from philosophical and psychological perspectives. Topics include fairness and bias, privacy, responsibility, accountability, the moral status of AI systems and broader political risks. Students also consider trust and decision-making, empathy and confidentiality in clinical settings, algorithmic stereotypes, and how AI companions and tutors may affect children’s learning and relationships.
Close

Decision-making in AI
Introduces planning techniques for AI systems in deterministic and non‑deterministic environments. Addresses uncertainty, partial observability, resource planning and optimizing behaviour under constraints.
Close

Optimization Methods in AI
Optimization Methods in AI studies search and optimisation for rational agents. Topics include uninformed and informed search, local and global search, adversarial games and constraint satisfaction. Laboratory exercises and projects include graph search, convex optimisation, and linear and nonlinear programming.
Close

Introduction to Data Science
Develops foundational skills in data visualization, cleaning and manipulation. Explores spatial and text data and includes hands‑on work with datasets from various disciplines.
Close

Machine Learning
Machine Learning introduces methods for understanding data and making predictions, including linear regression, classification, resampling, shrinkage, tree-based methods, support vector machines and clustering. Real-world examples illustrate the methods, their strengths and limitations.
Close

Image Processing & Computer Vision
Image Processing & Computer Vision studies how structural information is extracted from images and video. Topics include camera and colour models, filtering, edge and feature detection, segmentation, tracking and object recognition. Practical work develops computational image-analysis skills, with applications including medical imaging and remote sensing.
Close

Neural Networks & Deep Learning
Neural Networks & Deep Learning combines theory with practical Python implementations. Students build and train networks, use TensorFlow, and study applications to tabular data, computer vision and text classification. Recent language-model developments are discussed; image-generation models may be considered if time permits.
Close

Introduction to Programming
Introduces programming and computer science. Covers structured programming, data constructs, testing, debugging and object‑oriented programming with Python, and develops computational problem‑solving skills.
Close

Mathematical Methods
Mathematical Methods develops foundational techniques in differentiation, integration, complex numbers and differential equations. Students solve mathematical problems and apply these techniques in projects drawing on fields such as science, economics and sociology.
Close

Climate Change
Focuses on drivers and impacts of anthropogenic climate change on sea level, ocean acidification, ecology and society. Discusses adaptation and mitigation solutions, including renewable energy systems, carbon storage and climate‑adaptive planning, and examines climate governance and justice.
Close

Philosophy of Mind
Examines historical and modern work on the philosophy of mind. Discusses Descartes’ dualism, the nature of consciousness, AI and animal minds, personal identity, transformative experiences and the influence of technology on experience.
Close

Introduction to Sociology
Introduces concepts, theories and methods of sociology. Examines socio‑historical context of key authors like Marx, Weber, Durkheim and Du Bois, and encourages exploration of social problems related to race, gender and class through theoretical approaches and methodologies.
Close

Qualitative Research Methodology
Introduces qualitative research methodology. Covers designing questions, interpreting meaning and conducting small team projects, while reflecting on complexity and power dynamics in social research.
Close

Modern Sociology
Examines the trajectory of sociology within the culture of imperialism and colonial responses. Studies leading social theories and debates about modernity and critically engages with sociological discourses.
Close

Social Movements & Environmental Justice
Focuses on social movement theories and environmental justice. Uses case studies from the Environmental Justice Atlas and integrates perspectives such as feminism, anti‑colonialism, degrowth and environmental peacebuilding to encourage civic engagement.
Close

New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory
Examines contemporary sociological debates about civil society through critical tradition, neo‑functionalism and decolonial critiques. Includes research group projects with NGOs or civil society organizations that translate conceptual insights into empirical analysis.
Close

Epidemiology & Public Health
Introduces epidemiology and the evidence used in public health. It examines disease patterns, risks and changes over time, and how research can inform decisions about population health.
Close

Psycholinguistics
Psycholinguistics is the study of the neurobiological and psychological factors that enable us to acquire, use, and understand language. Modern research draws on cognitive psychology, neuroscience, and computer science to investigate how language is processed. The course focuses primarily, though not exclusively, on the neuroscience of language. Students examine theoretical and experimental issues in speech production and comprehension, language impairments, the relationship between thought and language, and the evolution and acquisition of language. They also gain hands-on experience with experimental approaches to the study of language and develop an understanding of human linguistic capacity as a subject of multidisciplinary research. Topics covered: What is language? Evolutionary aspects of language and animal communication; language and thought; aphasia; language acquisition; bilingualism; speech comprehension; semantics; reading and dyslexia; speech production.
Close

Introduction to Brain & Behavior
Explores why people behave as they do and how brain injuries affect mental processes. Discusses nature and nurture, introduces brain anatomy and psychological theories, and provides a gateway to cognitive science and clinical psychology.
Close

Social Psychology
Covers main theories, findings and principles of social psychology, emphasising its scientific approach to understanding how people’s feelings, thoughts and behaviour are influenced by the presence of others.
Close

Statistics & Experimental Methods
Teaches multivariate statistical methods for research on complex human phenomena. Topics include linear and logistic regression, factor analysis, analysis of variance and covariance, and non-parametric tests. Students select and apply models, assess statistical problems and report their analyses.
Close

The Art of Rhetorical Communication
The Art of Rhetorical Communication develops rhetorical analysis, academic writing and oral presentation. Students examine classical Western roots and the canons of rhetoric, and learn to construct, organise and support persuasive arguments. Historical and contemporary examples connect rhetorical theory with practical communication.
Close

Style & Meaning
Style & Meaning studies stylistics: how linguistic choices produce meaning and interpretive effects, principally in literary texts. Students analyse language from phonetic and discourse levels to cognition, applying theoretical frameworks to fictional and selected nonfiction texts.
Close

Communicating the Climate Crisis
Examines how the climate crisis is communicated and contested. Analyzes texts, films, exhibitions, protest art, slogans and social media alongside theory and case studies, teaching students to dissect arguments and culminating in a project where students enter the debate.
Close

Rhetoric in Action
Develops persuasive speaking skills by applying rhetorical theory in the real world. Students work with local primary school children, building public-speaking skills and empowering them to find their voices.
Close

Persuasive Communication
Persuasive Communication builds on classical rhetoric and argumentation to study persuasion in science, society and sustainability. Students examine framing, nudging, cognitive shortcuts and ethical approaches to persuasion. In a community-engaged project, they help local institutions address communication challenges.
Close

Creative Communication Laboratory
Creative Communication Laboratory combines critical reading, theory, discussion and reflective writing with poetry, rhythm, sound, voice and performance. Students develop poetic and hybrid creative projects. Singing, songwriting and music performance are excluded; sound must function as poetic, linguistic or conceptual material.
Close

Introduction to Film & Media
Introduction to Film & Media focuses primarily on cinema history, film culture and analysis. Students study narrative, cinematography, editing and sound, examine influential films in their theoretical and political contexts, and engage with academic readings. The final part briefly connects film to television, streaming and digital platforms.
Close

Media Archaeology
Explores media technologies before digital culture. Studies cassette tapes, typewriters and early printing as material objects that carry meaning; includes hands‑on experiments; no technical background required.
Close

From T.V. to TikTok
From T.V. to TikTok examines American social history and everyday life through mainstream media from the mid-twentieth century to the present. Television, film, podcasts and social media reveal how storytelling constructs identity and possible futures. Native American and disability representation illustrate how media can marginalise and empower people.
Close

Media & the Environment
Examines representation of environmental concerns through visual culture. Explores the Anthropocene, animal representation, deep time, biocentrism, contested nature, indigenous and postcolonial media; analyzes how media shape environmental understanding; and includes a paper or media project.
Close

Media & Race
Media & Race investigates storytelling, power, privilege, resistance and systemic racism in American history from the late nineteenth century to the present. Film, photographs, music and other media connect past and present. Students produce research-based podcasts exploring how media sustains oppression and supports resistance.
Close

Close

Decision-making in AI
Introduces planning techniques for AI systems in deterministic and non‑deterministic environments. Addresses uncertainty, partial observability, resource planning and optimizing behaviour under constraints.
Close

Optimization Methods in AI
Optimization Methods in AI studies search and optimisation for rational agents. Topics include uninformed and informed search, local and global search, adversarial games and constraint satisfaction. Laboratory exercises and projects include graph search, convex optimisation, and linear and nonlinear programming.
Close

Introduction to Data Science
Develops foundational skills in data visualization, cleaning and manipulation. Explores spatial and text data and includes hands‑on work with datasets from various disciplines.
Close

Machine Learning
Machine Learning introduces methods for understanding data and making predictions, including linear regression, classification, resampling, shrinkage, tree-based methods, support vector machines and clustering. Real-world examples illustrate the methods, their strengths and limitations.
Close

Image Processing & Computer Vision
Image Processing & Computer Vision studies how structural information is extracted from images and video. Topics include camera and colour models, filtering, edge and feature detection, segmentation, tracking and object recognition. Practical work develops computational image-analysis skills, with applications including medical imaging and remote sensing.
Close

Neural Networks & Deep Learning
Neural Networks & Deep Learning combines theory with practical Python implementations. Students build and train networks, use TensorFlow, and study applications to tabular data, computer vision and text classification. Recent language-model developments are discussed; image-generation models may be considered if time permits.
Close

Introduction to Programming
Introduces programming and computer science. Covers structured programming, data constructs, testing, debugging and object‑oriented programming with Python, and develops computational problem‑solving skills.
Close

Mathematical Methods
Mathematical Methods develops foundational techniques in differentiation, integration, complex numbers and differential equations. Students solve mathematical problems and apply these techniques in projects drawing on fields such as science, economics and sociology.
Close

Climate Change
Focuses on drivers and impacts of anthropogenic climate change on sea level, ocean acidification, ecology and society. Discusses adaptation and mitigation solutions, including renewable energy systems, carbon storage and climate‑adaptive planning, and examines climate governance and justice.
Close

Philosophy of Mind
Examines historical and modern work on the philosophy of mind. Discusses Descartes’ dualism, the nature of consciousness, AI and animal minds, personal identity, transformative experiences and the influence of technology on experience.
Close

Introduction to Sociology
Introduces concepts, theories and methods of sociology. Examines socio‑historical context of key authors like Marx, Weber, Durkheim and Du Bois, and encourages exploration of social problems related to race, gender and class through theoretical approaches and methodologies.
Close

Qualitative Research Methodology
Introduces qualitative research methodology. Covers designing questions, interpreting meaning and conducting small team projects, while reflecting on complexity and power dynamics in social research.
Close

Modern Sociology
Examines the trajectory of sociology within the culture of imperialism and colonial responses. Studies leading social theories and debates about modernity and critically engages with sociological discourses.
Close

Social Movements & Environmental Justice
Focuses on social movement theories and environmental justice. Uses case studies from the Environmental Justice Atlas and integrates perspectives such as feminism, anti‑colonialism, degrowth and environmental peacebuilding to encourage civic engagement.
Close

New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory
Examines contemporary sociological debates about civil society through critical tradition, neo‑functionalism and decolonial critiques. Includes research group projects with NGOs or civil society organizations that translate conceptual insights into empirical analysis.
Close

Epidemiology & Public Health
Introduces epidemiology and the evidence used in public health. It examines disease patterns, risks and changes over time, and how research can inform decisions about population health.
Close

Psycholinguistics
Psycholinguistics is the study of the neurobiological and psychological factors that enable us to acquire, use, and understand language. Modern research draws on cognitive psychology, neuroscience, and computer science to investigate how language is processed. The course focuses primarily, though not exclusively, on the neuroscience of language. Students examine theoretical and experimental issues in speech production and comprehension, language impairments, the relationship between thought and language, and the evolution and acquisition of language. They also gain hands-on experience with experimental approaches to the study of language and develop an understanding of human linguistic capacity as a subject of multidisciplinary research. Topics covered: What is language? Evolutionary aspects of language and animal communication; language and thought; aphasia; language acquisition; bilingualism; speech comprehension; semantics; reading and dyslexia; speech production.
Close

Introduction to Brain & Behavior
Explores why people behave as they do and how brain injuries affect mental processes. Discusses nature and nurture, introduces brain anatomy and psychological theories, and provides a gateway to cognitive science and clinical psychology.
Close

Social Psychology
Covers main theories, findings and principles of social psychology, emphasising its scientific approach to understanding how people’s feelings, thoughts and behaviour are influenced by the presence of others.
Close

Statistics & Experimental Methods
Teaches multivariate statistical methods for research on complex human phenomena. Topics include linear and logistic regression, factor analysis, analysis of variance and covariance, and non-parametric tests. Students select and apply models, assess statistical problems and report their analyses.
Close

The Art of Rhetorical Communication
The Art of Rhetorical Communication develops rhetorical analysis, academic writing and oral presentation. Students examine classical Western roots and the canons of rhetoric, and learn to construct, organise and support persuasive arguments. Historical and contemporary examples connect rhetorical theory with practical communication.
Close

Style & Meaning
Style & Meaning studies stylistics: how linguistic choices produce meaning and interpretive effects, principally in literary texts. Students analyse language from phonetic and discourse levels to cognition, applying theoretical frameworks to fictional and selected nonfiction texts.
Close

Communicating the Climate Crisis
Examines how the climate crisis is communicated and contested. Analyzes texts, films, exhibitions, protest art, slogans and social media alongside theory and case studies, teaching students to dissect arguments and culminating in a project where students enter the debate.
Close

Rhetoric in Action
Develops persuasive speaking skills by applying rhetorical theory in the real world. Students work with local primary school children, building public-speaking skills and empowering them to find their voices.
Close

Persuasive Communication
Persuasive Communication builds on classical rhetoric and argumentation to study persuasion in science, society and sustainability. Students examine framing, nudging, cognitive shortcuts and ethical approaches to persuasion. In a community-engaged project, they help local institutions address communication challenges.
Close

Creative Communication Laboratory
Creative Communication Laboratory combines critical reading, theory, discussion and reflective writing with poetry, rhythm, sound, voice and performance. Students develop poetic and hybrid creative projects. Singing, songwriting and music performance are excluded; sound must function as poetic, linguistic or conceptual material.
Close

Introduction to Film & Media
Introduction to Film & Media focuses primarily on cinema history, film culture and analysis. Students study narrative, cinematography, editing and sound, examine influential films in their theoretical and political contexts, and engage with academic readings. The final part briefly connects film to television, streaming and digital platforms.
Close

Media Archaeology
Explores media technologies before digital culture. Studies cassette tapes, typewriters and early printing as material objects that carry meaning; includes hands‑on experiments; no technical background required.
Close

From T.V. to TikTok
From T.V. to TikTok examines American social history and everyday life through mainstream media from the mid-twentieth century to the present. Television, film, podcasts and social media reveal how storytelling constructs identity and possible futures. Native American and disability representation illustrate how media can marginalise and empower people.
Close

Media & the Environment
Examines representation of environmental concerns through visual culture. Explores the Anthropocene, animal representation, deep time, biocentrism, contested nature, indigenous and postcolonial media; analyzes how media shape environmental understanding; and includes a paper or media project.
Close

Media & Race
Media & Race investigates storytelling, power, privilege, resistance and systemic racism in American history from the late nineteenth century to the present. Film, photographs, music and other media connect past and present. Students produce research-based podcasts exploring how media sustains oppression and supports resistance.
Close
